title: "Tiny Machine Learning"

TinyML connects machine learning with the constraints of embedded devices:
collecting sensor data, training compact models, and deploying them on
microcontrollers. This page brings together the original Harvard course websites
and public repositories associated with CS249r.

The original sites remain the record of each offering's schedule, staff, and
assessment. These historical courses helped shape the broader ML systems
curriculum; their original names and materials are preserved here.

## Past Harvard offerings

- **[Fall 2023: CS249r Tiny Machine Learning](https://sites.google.com/g.harvard.edu/cs249-tinyml-2023/home).**
  The course site describes the class's collaborative work on an early
  *Introduction to Machine Learning Systems for TinyML* book. It also hosts a
  [final-project showcase](https://sites.google.com/g.harvard.edu/cs249-tinyml-2023/fall-2023-final-projects).
- **[Fall 2022: CS249r Tiny Machine Learning](https://sites.google.com/g.harvard.edu/tinyml/home).**
  The graduate seminar's original homepage, with course information and a linked
  syllabus. Its URL does not include the year; the page identifies the offering
  as Fall 2022. A [project showcase](https://sites.google.com/g.harvard.edu/cs249-tinyml-2023/fall-2022-final-projects)
  is preserved on the later course site.
- **[Fall 2020: CS249r Tiny Machine Learning](https://sites.google.com/g.harvard.edu/tinyml-fall2020/home).**
  The original course website, with Vijay Janapa Reddi and Pete Warden listed as
  instructors, and Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense as the development platform.

## Course assignments on GitHub

- **[CS249r course repository](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r).**
  The Harvard Edge repository links the early book and semester assignment
  repositories through its
  [submodule configuration](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r/blob/main/.gitmodules).
- **[Fall 2020 assignment seed](https://github.com/Harvard-CS249R-Fall2020/assignments).**
  Public assignment starters for hello world, gesture recognition, person
  detection, wake words, and responsible AI. The repository includes the original
  GitHub Classroom workflow used by the course.
- **[Fall 2022 Assignment 2](https://github.com/mmaz/cs249r-a2).**
  The repository identifies the semester in its README and is linked from the
  course repository. It contains the assignment notebook, training and
  quantization scripts, and deployment resources for visual wake words/person
  detection. [Open its notebook in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/mmaz/cs249r-a2/blob/master/cs249r_a2.ipynb).

## Selected public student projects

These links lead to student-maintained repositories. They provide examples of
complete projects, including data collection, training, and hardware deployment.

### Cache 4 Trash

[Project repository](https://github.com/AditiR-42/cache-4-trash) ·
[Course showcase](https://sites.google.com/g.harvard.edu/cs249-tinyml-2023/fall-2023-final-projects)

Sophia Cho, Jared Ni, and Aditi Raju's project combines waste classification on
Nicla Vision with a motorized sorting mechanism. The repository includes dataset
preparation, augmentation, model deployment, firmware, and hardware diagrams.
The course's 2023 showcase identifies the project and its authors.

### Activity recognition and ultrasound power control

[Project repository](https://github.com/euranofshin/ultrasound-power-tinyml)

The repository explicitly identifies itself as a Harvard CS249R 2023 final
project. Its README documents activity data, a Nicla Vision inference sketch,
experiment plotting scripts, and the connection to an ultrasound system.

### Air Guitar

[Project repository](https://github.com/RobJMal/Air-Guitar-CS249R)

The repository identifies this as a Harvard CS249R final project. It combines
motion and finger-flex sensing with learned gesture recognition on a Teensy
board, and includes collection code, training notebooks, deployment code, and
hardware schematics. The README does not specify the semester.

## Related HarvardX TinyML materials

The HarvardX/edX specialization is a separate teaching program. Its public
materials complement the campus course archive:

- **[TinyMLx courseware](https://github.com/tinyMLx/courseware/tree/master/edX):**
  course structure, slides, and readings for the HarvardX specialization.
- **[TinyMLx Colab notebooks](https://github.com/tinyMLx/colabs):** notebooks for
  the edX TinyML specialization.
- **[Harvard TinyMLx Arduino library](https://github.com/tinyMLx/arduino-library):**
  source code and examples for the TinyML kit and shield.

The [TinyMLedu teaching page](https://tinyml.seas.harvard.edu/teach/) connects
these materials with the Harvard campus offerings and a wider teaching community.

## Using these resources today

For the current textbook, start with [MLSysBook](https://mlsysbook.ai/).
For reusable teaching plans, visit the
[Instructor Hub](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/). To explore courses at other
institutions, use the
[community course directory](https://mlsysbook.ai/courses/).

*Resource links and course connections reviewed October 21, 2026. Historical
code and hardware instructions have not been rerun against current toolchains.*
